title: Count the shelf, write a report
prompt:
Ms. Gridlock wants one number: how many parts sit on the shelf. The file `parts.csv` (fictional) lists each part with its `qty`. Add up the `qty` column, then write the answer into a new file named `report.txt`.

Keep `parts.csv` in the same folder as `report.py`, and run the commands from that folder. A file name with no folder in front is a relative path, so Python looks for it in the current working directory [py-005].

When it works, `report.txt` holds one line, `Total parts: 100`, and the program prints the same line.
hints: Each `row` is a dictionary. `row["qty"]` gives you the quantity, as text such as `"30"`.
Text and numbers do not add. Turn the text into a whole number first: `int(row["qty"])`. Then add it to `total`.
For the report, open a second file with `with open("report.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as out:` and call `out.write("Total parts: " + str(total) + "\n")` inside it.
explain_after:
`csv.DictReader` turned each row into a dictionary keyed by the header names [py-162]. Mode `'w'` writes a file and erases anything that was there before [py-101], and `f.write(string)` puts your text in it [py-103]. The `with` block closed both files for you [py-102].

Open `report.txt` in VS Code to see what your program made. Run the program twice: the file still holds one line, because `'w'` starts fresh each time.
